newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies expected lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies expected lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.200 cent per lb lower while pork bellies were called 0.200 to 0.500 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Steady to lower cash hog indications and another decline in cutout values were expected to prompt carryover pressure in hog futures. Packer margins are well in the red and they continue to cut slaughter rates and reduce bids for cash hogs, analysts said.
Product demand has been light despite the light pace of slaughter as high prices cut off both domestic and export demand last week, they said.

Carryover selling from Friday's sharply lower to near limit losses was expected in pork belly futures following further weakness in cash product last week despite the light pace of slaughter. Cash bellies declined $2 to $5 per cwt on Friday and prices fell $7 during the week, analysts said.

The market turned technically weak after falling through the 10-day moving average late in the week and slipping to two week lows. There is also some nervousness expected over deliveries on first notice day. First notices will be posted later Monday afternoon, they added.
